properties.version_basis: PDF identified by SHA-256 against assignments.json; title page read.

properties.description: Multi-step latent action model with a fine-tuned video diffusion dynamics model for action transfer across surgical contexts.
Latent action encoder with a composite multi-step latent action and a fine-tuned Stable Video Diffusion dynamics model that generates frames from a context frame and transferred actions.

properties.algorithm: Multi-step latent action model with SVD video diffusion dynamics

properties.population: public surgical videos (SurgToolLoc robotic training, PitVis endoscopic pituitary surgery)
properties.decision: transfer of demonstrated actions to a new target context for simulation and training

properties.algorithm: Discrete autoregressive LAM with multi-step dynamics

capability_assessments.rationale: SurgTransfer implements block-generated 7-frame multi-step prediction with frame-7 state carry-over to horizon 14 (state.persistent), learned temporal diffusion dynamics (dynamics.temporal, dynamics.learned_hybrid), and latent-action-conditioned future prediction evaluated on SurgToolLoc and PitVis with quantitative video metrics and five-surgeon plausibility ratings (L2). Actions are unsupervised latent encodings rather than ground-truth kinematics or causally identified interventions, and all evaluations are retrospective.

SurgTransfer implements block-generated 7-frame multi-step prediction with frame-7 state carry-over to horizon 14 (state.persistent), learned temporal diffusion dynamics (dynamics.temporal, dynamics.learned_hybrid), and latent-action-conditioned future prediction evaluated on SurgToolLoc and PitVis with quantitative video metrics and five-surgeon plausibility ratings (L2). Actions are unsupervised latent encodings rather than ground-truth kinematics or causally identified interventions, and all evaluations are retrospective.

gate_assessments.rationale: The split of training and test videos is not stated in the text read, and the two source and target segments of one clip may share content.

Future-frame reconstruction and transfer are evaluated against baselines (Tables 2-3, Fig. 6a), but G02 remains unresolved because G01 non-leaky video/subject-level split verification is unresolved (80:20 split granularity is unstated and SurgToolLoc transfer pairs split a single 30 s clip), action transfer lacks ground-truth target videos, and reconstruction outcomes are mixed across baselines (optical flow lower CD-FVD; discrete AR lower CMMD).

legacy_cells.C: Koju, Saurabh, Panta, Love, Thapa, Deepak, Poudel, Rudra P. K., Ghimire, Prajwal, Watson, Angus, et al.
legacy_cells.O: Robot-assisted surgical training exercises; endoscopic pituitary surgeries
legacy_cells.S: Can composite latent actions inferred from a source surgical video generate future frames in a different surgical context while preserving action semantics?
legacy_cells.AI: Surgical video frames: source video clips and a target-context frame
legacy_cells.AJ: ST-Transformer latent-action encoder/decoder; Stable Video Diffusion UNet for dynamics
legacy_cells.AK: Stable Video Diffusion (SVD), publicly available image-to-video model, fine-tuned
legacy_cells.BD: Continuous 32-dimensional latent action representations; action posterior parameterized by (μ, σ) and sampled
legacy_cells.BL: Training window size 8 frames; reported prediction horizon 14 frames
legacy_cells.BS: Generated future surgical video frames conditioned on a context frame and transferred latent actions
legacy_cells.BV: LAM: future-frame reconstruction squared error plus β-weighted KL divergence to a standard normal; dynamics: diffusion denoising squared error
legacy_cells.DQ: SurgToolLoc-2022: 24,695 video clips; PitVis: 25 videos, average length over one hour
legacy_cells.DZ: Action-transfer evaluation: CD-FVD was reported lower by 58% on SurgToolLoc and 69% on PitVis for the proposed LAM models; CD-FVD and embedding cosine similarity were evaluated.
legacy_cells.EA: Five-level expert plausibility ratings (SurgTransfer): visual perceptual 3.42 ± 0.35; instrument operation 3.27 ± 0.37; environment feedback 3.31 ± 0.34; surgical intent 3.23 ± 0.35; action transfer 3.15 ± 0.38.
legacy_cells.EE: Five certified surgeons independently rated 40 generated videos using a questionnaire covering visual, instrument, environment, surgical-intent, and action-transfer plausibility; mean inter-rater ICC(2,k) was 0.54 for SurgTransfer.
legacy_cells.EG: Generation: 3.61 seconds for 7 frames (1.94 FPS) on one NVIDIA L40 GPU; peak VRAM 15.43 GB. LAM training: 100k steps on 2 NVIDIA A100 GPUs; diffusion fine-tuning: 80k steps on 8 NVIDIA L40 GPUs.
legacy_cells.EJ: Compared with AdaWorld: SurgTransfer scored higher on all five expert plausibility levels; action-transfer CD-FVD was reported lower by 58% on SurgToolLoc and 69% on PitVis.
legacy_cells.EK: Ablated LAM context length K=2–16; compared autoregressive and multi-step dynamics; compared autoregressive, AdaWorld, multi-step, discrete, and optical-flow action variants.
legacy_cells.EL: The authors report deterioration as prediction horizon increases, a sudden quality drop at generated frame 8 when the context resets after frame 7, and over-amplification of source movements in a trajectory example. They also show AdaWorld instrument disappearance and faster quality fall-off.
legacy_cells.FB: Visual state is represented by a surgical context frame/video; a causal ST-Transformer LAM infers a sampled 32-dimensional continuous latent-action sequence, and a fine-tuned Stable Video Diffusion model generates future video conditioned on the context and actions; no planner is implemented.
legacy_cells.FL: ST-Transformer encoder infers a continuous latent-action sequence from a source clip; an ST-Transformer decoder reconstructs future frames during LAM training; a fine-tuned Stable Video Diffusion UNet predicts future video conditioned on the target context frame and transferred actions; no task head or planner.
legacy_cells.FM: Introduces SurgTransfer, a surgical procedure-transfer framework, and a multi-step latent-action model that learns composable, context-invariant actions from unlabeled surgical videos; evaluates action transfer quantitatively and with surgical experts.
legacy_cells.FN: On cross-context transfer, reported CD-FVD reductions were 58% on SurgToolLoc and 69% on PitVis for the proposed LAM models. Expert ratings for SurgTransfer ranged from 3.15 ± 0.38 (action transfer) to 3.42 ± 0.35 (visual perceptual plausibility); ICC(2,k)=0.54.
legacy_cells.FO: The framework is limited to surgical contexts with similar anatomy or view, the same procedure, and the same instrument embodiment. Its unsupervised setting offers limited insight into downstream performance where ground-truth actions are available. A pre-defined latent-action trajectory prevents a truly interactive experience.
legacy_cells.FP: The authors propose adapting the models to action spaces of specialized surgical tasks.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors state that prior surgical latent-action models infer actions between consecutive frames and are myopic for hierarchical, goal-directed procedures; transferring latent actions across surgical contexts had been unexplored.
legacy_cells.FR: The study demonstrates retrospective video generation/action transfer and expert plausibility ratings, not identified treatment effects, executable robot control, interactive planning, prospective clinical performance, or patient/workflow benefit. The authors explicitly state that the pre-defined action trajectory prevents a truly interactive experience.

notes:
SurgTransfer learns a composite multi-step latent action from unlabeled surgical video and conditions a fine-tuned Stable Video Diffusion model to transfer it to a new context frame. Transfer CD-FVD falls from 341.76 to 141.41 on SurgToolLoc and from 513.27 to 157.34 on PitVis against AdaWorld, and five surgeons rate 40 videos higher on all five plausibility levels (2.6 to 3.1-3.4 of an unstated scale maximum) with ICC about 0.5. Classified L2, supporting component. Source points: no carried state, latent actions uninterpreted, split not stated, single runs, one baseline family, limited to similar anatomy.

Targeted source gap-review addendum (2026-11-22): Figures 1-3 show composable multi-step latent action inference and an action-conditioned diffusion dynamics model. Figures 7-9 show qualitative source-to-target action transfer, including appearance transfer; these are selected examples, not new outcome evidence. Figure 5 was visually read: context/reset lengths 2,4,8,12,16 have decreasing CD-FVD and increasing ECS. The plot has axis ticks but no numeric point labels, so exact ordinate values are not transcribed or estimated. Figures 10-11, omitted from the old inventory, occur on physical pages 14-15. Figure 10 includes an initial displacement mismatch despite close later tracking; Figure 11 explicitly shows over-amplification of source movement. Algorithms 1-3 on page 13 were read; Algorithm 3 resets target context to the last generated frame for subsequent blocks. References 1-45 were reviewed as entries only. Repository and external videos were not inspected.
